DEPUTATIONS
Item 8.1:
Victor Sagar, deputant, requested clarification on items related to the Housing Accelerator Fund, particularly surrounding Council's decision to not allow four units per residential property, as of right. Mr. Sagar also requested that building permits in process be posted online for public view. The Committee provided clarification on the process undertaken surrounding the four-unit permissions and underscored Council's focus on achieving the best possible scenarios. Stephanie Mezzone, Chief Building Official, confirmed that all in progress building permits are available on the City's website.
Item 13.1.4:
Frank Yam, deputant and area resident, expressed opposition to the construction of the sports dome and concerns about the impact on the surrounding residential area including area traffic and fire safety.
Jennifer McInnis, deputant, expressed concerns with the size of the dome and the greenspace being blocked from the school windows and the homes. Ms. McInnis noted that the application failed before the Committee of Adjustment and expressed her hope that a different location be considered. Ms. McInnis added that she contacted the York Catholic District School Board trusee but has not received a response.
Jian Huan Yeo, deputant, expressed opposition to the sports dome, expressing that she does not feel it is an appropriate location.
Yufei Liu, deputant, echoed the concerns of the other deputants, emphasizing safety and noise concerns.
Rainbow Choi, deputant, expressed strong opposition to proposed sports dome related to concerns about noise, lighting, and increased traffic.
Kio Ung, deputant, expressed concerns about the safety of the dome and potential collapse due to snow. , who would be responsible for the loss of human lives if anything goes wrong.
Sok I Lo, deputant, expressed opposition to the proposed sports dome, expressing concerns about the traffic and location.
John Butcher, deputant, expressed concern with the proposed sports dome and asked that the City support the Committee of Adjustment decision at the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing. Mr. Butcher added that studies including a sun and shade study were not undertaken by the Applicant.
Bing D Gan, deputant, expressed opposition to the dome due to its size and asked that the City to maintain its position at the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing.
Junlei Yu, deputant, expressed concern about the notice provided related to this item.
The Committee clarified the process to date, explaining that the application was turned down by the Committee of Adjustment, in line with concerns of the area residents but the application is now being appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The Committee encouraged area residents to contact the Provincially appointed supervisor of the York Catholic District School Board as well as the trustee. The Committee advised residents that if they made a deputation to the Committee of Adjustment on this matter, they could join the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing taking place on November 18, 2026 as a participant.

Mayor Frank Scarpitti

Giulio Cescato, Director, introduced this item as an update on the City's progress with respect to the Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) and introduced Audrey Farias to provide a presentation.
Audrey Farias, Project Manager, Housing Accelerator Fund, delivered a presentation.
The Committee discussed the following:
Asked about the impact of missing one commitment, when every other target had been met. Ms. Farias advised that there was a $7M reduction to funding as a result of missing that commitment. Director Cescato added that the funding was reallocated from other projects, minimizing the overall impact.
Sought clarification on the source of the $9M allocated to consultants, salaries, and legal fees. Director Cescato confirmed that these were items allocated for in the HAF budget from the outset, noting that no additional costs were realized throughout the process.
Asked if the program was beneficial to the City overall. Director Cescato expressed that he thought HAF to be an excellent program, with a majority of the funding going toward building new units.
Asked why the program is being ended considering the successes. Ms. Farias clarified that there is a divided opinion among municipalities, with some noting that the policies were stifling as it required adherence to the milestones and reporting structure.
Asked if Staff still supports the projects selected for funding and the level of funding they each received. Director Cescato confirmed that Staff supports the process undertaken and agreements put in place to secure funding. Nadia Lawrence, Special Project Coordinator, explained the process undertaken and the scoring metrics required by the City to determine if a project should qualify for funding.
Moved by
Mayor Frank Scarpitti
Seconded by
Councillor Keith Irish
That the report dated, November 3, 2026, titled “CMHC Housing Accelerator Fund Update”, be received; and,
That Staff be authorized and directed to do all things necessary to give effect to this resolution.
Carried

Giulio Cescato, Director, Planning & Urban Design, introduced this item as Official Plan amendment and Zoning By-law amendment applications to permit a mixed-use development, consisting of 987 residential units, non-residential uses, and a public park. Director Cescato introduced Maria Gatzios to deliver a presentation.
Maria Gatzios, Gatzios Planning, delivered a presentation. Caroline Richard, architect, provided additional comments.
The Committee discussed the following:
Sought clarification on the amount of parkland being achieved at this site. Ms. Gatzios advised that for, Phase 2, the parkland is an over-dedication, and that for the overall development, the parkland conveyance is close to what is required. Stephen Corr, Senior Planner, Development, noted that the overall under-dedication would need to be reconciled.
Asked about the status of the proposed pedestrian bride. Frank Clarizio, Director, Engineering, advised that the Applicant no longer wishes to provide a pedestrian bridge due to the signalized pedestrian walkway at the intersection. Director Clarizio confirmed that Staff would continue to work with the Applicant to see if there is a way to connect the two developments, whether above or below grade, which is not currently required but would be an enhancement. Director Cescato added that there is not a mechanism to require the pedestrian bridge.
Asked if purchasers of the units were told that there would be a pedestrian bridge. Ms. Gatzios advised that while it may have been in some conceptual renderings, it was not committed to.
Expressed disappointment of the parkland being provided considering the number of units and asked that the item go to Council in December to provide time for continued discussions with the Applicant.

Seconded by
